design_summary.purpose: Demonstrate prebuilt Sky130 SRAM macro integration with a small 256x32 scratchpad controller and MBIST-facing collateral while keeping a synthesizable fallback path available for flows where the macro collateral is not present.
design_summary.operating_model: The controller accepts software-visible read/write requests, manages a simple register map for memory access and BIST control/status, and drives a single functional SRAM wrapper interface. The wrapper binds either to the prebuilt Sky130 SRAM macro sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 or to a synthesizable model with the same interface. BIST status and IRQ signaling remain present in the controller regardless of downstream MBIST wrapping.

module_architecture.name: sram_mbist_demo_controller
module_architecture.role: Top-level memory-test reference controller and register-facing software interface.
responsibilities: Expose the external control/status ports exactly as specified.
Implement the register map at 0x00 through 0x24 for control, status, memory access, BIST control/status, and IRQ management.
Serialize simple scratchpad read/write accesses to the child memory wrapper using the wrapper's clk, csb, web, addr[7:0], din[31:0], and dout[31:0] interface semantics.
Track ready, busy, bist_done, bist_fail, last_fail_addr, and IRQ state as software-visible controller status.
Accept a BIST request through bist_start and the BIST_CONTROL.START register bit while preserving BIST status registers for downstream MBIST replacement or wrapping.
Drive irq when IRQ_ENABLE is set and latched BIST completion/failure status is present.
Keep the design synthesizable and suitable for downstream DFT/MBIST collateral generation.
interface_notes: The top module is a controller, not a raw SRAM model.
The top module instantiates demo_sram_32x256_wrapper as child memory wrapper instance u_sram.
The controller owns the software register map and exposes the memory intent to synthesis/DFT tools through the wrapper boundary.
ownership_notes: No ports or module names are redefined.
The wrapper instance name u_sram is preserved as required by the memory macro contract.
The prebuilt macro sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 is the targeted implementation when available, with demo_sram_32x256_model as fallback through the same wrapper interface.

module_architecture.name: demo_sram_32x256_wrapper
module_architecture.role: Functional scratchpad wrapper that presents a stable memory interface for either the prebuilt Sky130 SRAM macro or the synthesizable fallback model.
responsibilities: Provide the exact clk, csb, web, addr[7:0], din[31:0], dout[31:0] interface required for macro binding and MBIST tool recognition.
Bind to sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 when macro collateral is available.
Bind to demo_sram_32x256_model when collateral is unavailable at RTL generation time.
Preserve a single functional access path for the controller while keeping the second read port of the underlying macro safely tied off or reserved for MBIST wrapper integration.
interface_notes: The wrapper interface must remain stable for replacement or wrapping by AutoMBIST.
The controller uses one functional access path through this wrapper.
The wrapper instance under the controller is named u_sram as required.
ownership_notes: This module exists to make memory intent explicit.
It is the integration seam between controller logic and memory implementation choice.

module_architecture.name: demo_sram_32x256_model
module_architecture.role: Synthesizable fallback memory model used only when the prebuilt macro collateral is not available.
responsibilities: Implement a 256-word by 32-bit synchronous scratchpad behavior using generic RTL constructs only.
Match the wrapper port list exactly so the wrapper interface remains unchanged.
Remain synthesis-friendly and compatible with downstream replacement or wrapping by AutoMBIST and DFT flows.
Provide deterministic functional access for simulation and synthesis fallback purposes while leaving memory initialization unspecified unless explicitly initialized for test.
interface_notes: This is a fallback implementation, not a replacement for the top controller.
It preserves the exact wrapper interface to keep tool insertion points stable.
No vendor-only primitives are used in the fallback path.
ownership_notes: The fallback model does not change hierarchy at the top level.
The model preserves the same semantics expected by the wrapper contract and memory macro contract.

interface_summary.intent: Controller issues functional scratchpad accesses through the wrapper so the memory implementation can be either the prebuilt Sky130 macro or the synthesizable model without changing the top-level controller interface.
When macro collateral is available, the wrapper binds directly to the prebuilt SRAM macro to expose memory intent for synthesis and MBIST collateral generation.
When macro collateral is unavailable, the wrapper binds to the synthesizable fallback while keeping the same external memory contract for the controller and AutoMBIST flows.
Provide a simple software-facing control plane for scratchpad access, BIST initiation, BIST status reporting, and interrupt management.

data_flow_summary: Software writes MEM_ADDR and MEM_WDATA, then asserts MEM_CONTROL.MEM_WRITE to commit a write through the memory wrapper.
Software writes MEM_ADDR and asserts MEM_CONTROL.MEM_READ to request a read; the controller returns the addressed data via MEM_RDATA and rd_data.
The controller reflects BIST request activity from bist_start or BIST_CONTROL.START into internal BIST status tracking.
BIST completion or failure latches into BIST_STATUS and IRQ_STATUS, and irq is asserted only when IRQ_ENABLE is set and a latched BIST event is present.

Reset clears control and status-visible state, including ready, BIST status, IRQ status, and software-visible read data, while memory contents remain implementation-defined unless explicitly initialized for test.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: Single-clock synchronous design driven by clk across controller logic and the memory wrapper interface.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: reset_n is active-low. On reset, control/status registers, ready state, BIST status, IRQ state, and software-visible read data are cleared. The memory contents themselves may remain unspecified unless explicitly initialized for testing, but functional control signal behavior remains deterministic.

integration_notes: The memory intent is explicit through the named wrapper and the structured memory macro contract for sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8.
The design is intended to help downstream synthesis and DFT agents detect SRAM macro usage and generate MBIST collateral.
The controller preserves BIST status registers even if a later MBIST agent replaces or wraps the memory path.
The fallback model must remain synthesizable and use only generic RTL constructs.
The second read port of the underlying prebuilt SRAM is not used by the controller functional path and may be tied off safely or reserved for MBIST wrapper integration.

Packaging is expected to include synthesizable RTL, register map documentation, assertions, simulation testbench, UPF-lite collateral, timing constraints, and a manifest in the output file set named by the RTL output file contract.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
The top module remains sram_mbist_demo_controller and is not replaced by a raw SRAM model.
The memory macro contract names sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 and instance_name u_sram are preserved exactly.
